source_context_translations.translation: The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): a physical route or track used for travel or movement
additional_senses.Nuance (English): usually concrete and spatial, not abstract or moral
Sentence Translations (English): The cart travels on the road and proceeds without obstruction.
The traveling guest follows the path and goes on.
The old mountain road has long since become overgrown.
Returning at dusk, he lost the path and so asked someone.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): a guiding principle, procedure, or line of conduct for doing something, especially in governance, learning, or moral practice
additional_senses.Nuance (English): abstract but still practical; often implies a way of acting or governing rather than a mere technique
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; common philosophical and literary usage
Sentence Translations (English): There is a constant method for ruling the state.
The master transmits his teaching, and the students follow it.
The gentleman keeps to his course and does not change his resolve.
The way of warfare values judging the time correctly.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to utter words, state something, or refer to something verbally
additional_senses.Nuance (English): often means to state or speak about something explicitly
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; literary and common premodern usage
Sentence Translations (English): Everyone spoke of the matter.
I do not dare to mention its name.
The guest told the reason in person.
The historian records truthfully and does not speak falsely.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the ultimate, indefinable principle or source that underlies and orders reality; in the Laozi, the constant Way beyond ordinary speech
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): points to the ineffable cosmic Way, not a particular road or method
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension; philosophical

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): describes something as fitting, reasonable, or worth accepting as it stands
additional_senses.Nuance (English): stands alone as a judgment, not followed by a verb phrase
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; literary and common premodern usage
Sentence Translations (English): This plan is quite acceptable.
This statement is still not acceptable.
That proposal is also acceptable.
If it is like this, it is still acceptable.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to give approval or consent to someone or something, especially an official request or proposal
additional_senses.Nuance (English): takes an object and means to grant approval rather than to indicate ability
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; literary and official usage
Sentence Translations (English): The lord approved his request.
When the ruler had approved it, everyone was reassured.
The king did not approve this proposal.
The master heard his words and then assented.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): expresses possibility, permission, or ability for an action to be done
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): in this use it marks capability or permissibility before a verb
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension; common literary syntax

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): describes something as mistaken, improper, or not in accordance with what is true or right
additional_senses.Nuance (English): often evaluative, marking an asserted judgment of error
Sentence Translations (English): This claim is very wrong.
Much of his argument is mistaken.
That intention is indeed incorrect.
This action is not wrong.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to find fault with, denounce, or censure a person or action
additional_senses.Nuance (English): directs disapproval toward someone or something, often with a moral judgment
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; literary and moral discourse
Sentence Translations (English): Everyone criticized it.
One should not casually blame one’s friends.
Some scholars criticize my words.
If a lord can accept remonstrance, he should not lightly blame others.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): forms a negative predicate, denying that one thing is the same as, or falls under, another
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): here it negates identity or classification, not merely a verbal action
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension; common literary syntax
